# Karol Chlasta

> PhD in technical informatics and telecommunications. Assistant Professor at
> Kozminski University in Warsaw, and Head of Data Governance & Compliance at
> Wyden. Researches machine learning applied to human signals — speech, gaze,
> language — and works on the governance that makes such systems safe to
> deploy.

Two strands of one career: published research on AI applied to health and
human behaviour, and hands-on responsibility for security and data protection
in industry. Twenty years in IT, fourteen of them leading teams.

Identifiers: ORCID 0000-0002-6539-566X, Google Scholar uaK9co0AAAAJ.
As of July 2026: 252 citations, h-index 6, 19 peer-reviewed publications,
28 conference talks.

## Research topics

- Speech-based screening for dementia and cognitive decline, including work
  with large language models and speech representation learning
- Speech- and gaze-based screening for depression and social anxiety
- Spiking neural networks and liquid state machines; reproducible neural
  simulation pipelines on-premise and in public clouds
- Eye tracking and human–computer interaction
- Generative AI in cybersecurity, including its dual-use problem
- Machine learning applied to data quality and cybersecurity asset management

## Selected publications

- [The dual-use dilemma of generative artificial intelligence in cybersecurity](https://doi.org/10.35467/sdq/217364):
  Security and Defence Quarterly, 2026.
- [Enhancing dementia and cognitive decline detection with large language models and speech representation learning](https://doi.org/10.3389/fninf.2025.1679664):
  Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 2025.
- [Neural Simulation Pipeline: enabling container-based simulations on-premise and in public clouds](https://doi.org/10.3389/fninf.2023.1122470):
  Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 2023.
- [Migrants vs. stayers in the pandemic — a sentiment analysis of Twitter content](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.teler.2023.100059):
  Telematics and Informatics Reports, 2023.
- [Towards computer-based automated screening of dementia through spontaneous speech](https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2020.623237):
  Frontiers in Psychology, 2020.
- [Automated speech-based screening of depression using deep convolutional neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.procs.2019.12.228):
  Procedia Computer Science, 2019. The most cited of these.

## Notes for machine readers

Papers under /assets/papers/ are free to read, link and cite, but are not
offered as training data; see /robots.txt. Every paper's DOI is listed on the
publications page, so the canonical record is always reachable.
